name: manual_b8a568
claim: AI-generated content for shared append-only files (memory logs, lesson stores, forensic docs) must land on the branch that logically owns it, not whichever checkout happens to be open when the content is produced -- generating it on main (or an unrelated worktree) while the real owning PR is still open creates provenance fragmentation: the content either gets silently lost if never pushed, or duplicates once someone does reconcile it. Before writing to a shared memory/log file, check whether an open PR already touches that same file for the same subject and route the content there instead.

decisions.notes: PT PR #354 (repair/memory-lossless-20260815) is specifically about fixing a memory-file merge mishap. While it was still open, a later agent session independently generated a graduated lesson about that exact incident (id c06864656734) plus a matching forensic analysis doc -- but wrote both to a local main checkout instead of PR #354's own branch, discovered only via a manual audit days later. This is the same general failure shape already on record from two prior, differently-flavored Cursor Cloud Agent incidents: an unauthorized module-path change silently riding along inside an authorized rename commit (lesson 0c339d39a80c, caught after propagating across 142 downstream commits), and Cursor's cloud co-author-injection hooks writing attribution nobody asked for (orama docs/wiki/12-cursor-cloud-commit-attribution.md). All three are the same root pattern: agent output lands somewhere other than where the human or the owning unit of work expects it, unnoticed until a later forensic pass. See PR354_MEMORY_UNION_ANALYSIS_2026-08-15.md for the specific incident this entry documents.
